status: Sources, mechanical gates and internal contextual review passed; native review pending.
method: Original text panels, not copied manga. Japan Foundation, NINJAL and independent teacher/publisher explanations inform a media-recognition bridge. This is not an official N3 syllabus or a naturalness certificate.

points.formation: Attribute bubble lines to the labelled speaker; printed effects can describe sound, movement, state or feeling.
points.teachingChoice: NINJAL's detailed five-way classification is a reference, not a forced two-way taxonomy. One form may cross categories. The original panels label effects distinctly and do not assert that they were uttered.
points.sourceCaution: The Japan Foundation scene pages require interactive scripts; the instructions and notation pages were inspected, not falsely claimed as an audio audition.

points.form: Mimetic word and actual verb combination
points.formation: Selected combinations: じっと見る, にっこり笑う, どきどきする. Some use と; no universal transformation is taught.
points.teachingChoice: Words are taught with contextual action/state examples. ごろごろ at home and a thunder rumble are different uses. No claim that every mimetic takes する or represents audible sound.
points.sourceCaution: Maggie's simplified hiragana/katakana writing prescription is not treated as an absolute rule; manga spellings vary.

points.formation: A contextually recoverable object を or topic は can be omitted in familiar casual speech; explicit form practice restores the role.
points.teachingChoice: Recognise 傘見た？ without reversing the object and actor. Retain necessary relationship or contrast particles. No blanket instruction to omit particles or use this register in formal email.
points.sourceCaution: Mango's absolute ban on omitting point-in-time に and its mismatched emphasis example are not adopted. Maggie's own casually omitted を examples cross-check the narrow taught case.

points.form: Terminal small っ and expressive vowel length
points.formation: Terminal small っ indicates an abrupt cutoff; it is not separately pronounced つ. ー/〜 can represent an extended preceding vowel.
points.teachingChoice: Retrieve ordinary kana length/closure and distinguish short あっ from drawn-out あー. Expressive writing does not justify trailing extra sounds or arbitrary lengthening in kana drills.

points.formation: Question intonation/punctuation and reactions must be interpreted with the next reply or panel.
points.teachingChoice: A question about thunder does not establish thunder; relief follows the umbrella being found. Reactions and drawn tears/sweat do not uniquely identify their cause.
points.sourceCaution: Do not adopt absolute gender-only reaction claims or the prescription that every casual plain sentence must have an ending particle. Original tasks use explicit context and avoid those generalisations.

remaining: Native sentence/listening review; mechanical checks do not certify naturalness.
